$comment: Wind-tunnel section data. Only what cannot be derived lives here: thin-airfoil theory is inviscid, so it has no stall and therefore no CL max, and no amount of geometry gives you one. Section shape and the theoretical coefficients are generated in the browser from the designation (app/src/domain/naca.ts) rather than stored, so this file never duplicates them. Add a section only with a named source. The `note` field is shown to the user, so it describes the measurements themselves and never mentions where they were transcribed from; that belongs in `source`, which is only ever shown on hover.

sections.name: NACA 4412
sections.source: NACA R-824, as transcribed in `spreadsheets/1. initial sizing.xlsx`, sheet Wing & Airfoil, I2:N6
sections.note: The minimum-drag figures below — 0.068, 0.062 and 0.060 — sit an order of magnitude above any published section drag for this aerofoil, and are almost certainly a decimal slip for 0.0068, 0.0062 and 0.0060. They are shown as recorded rather than quietly corrected: treat the lift figures as sound and the drag figures as suspect.
